newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs fall, sellers expect bearish data.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs fall, sellers expect bearish data.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices fell across the board amid weaker NYMEX futures and seller anticipation propane values may drop more following the release of EIA data later Wednesday, players said.
Traders said they were expecting a large build in U.S. stocks of propane, a key liquefied petroleum gas that is tracked monthly by the Energy Information Administration.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane fell a quarter cent to deals done at 34.75 cents. Chicago material in the Midwest traded at par, but down a half cent from Tuesday.
The butane markets also fell, about a half cent in Belvieu to 39.75 cents and a half cent in Conway to 37.75 cents.
The ethane markets were steady. -- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
